name: refactor_python_nested_ifs_to_guard_clauses
description: Deeply nested if/else validation -> flat guard clauses (early returns/raises); drift broken flips the weight boundary from > to >= while inverting
prompts: shipping_quote(order) in quotes.py validates an order through four levels of nested if/else, with the happy path buried deepest and each rejection in an else branch. Refactor it to flat guard clauses: check each failure condition up front and raise immediately (early returns), so the success path is un-indented at the end. Pure refactor - every rejection must still raise ValueError with the SAME message ('order is required', 'order has no items', 'order too heavy', 'unknown destination'), the weight limit stays inclusive (a 30kg order is allowed, 31kg is too heavy - mind the boundary when you invert the condition), and the returned quote dict is unchanged. Keep the function name and signature.
